title: SC-2150 External video upload, YouTube import and human-behavior analysis
description:
Deliver bounded uploaded-video and supported YouTube import into Mouse Research, with immutable media/provenance, durable idempotent jobs, bounded probe/decode/cursor analysis, source-linked estimates and unknowns, append-only review, catalog inspection and evidence export. SC-2151 owns exact video-to-tick alignment; SC-309 owns movement diagnosis; SC-712 owns published training admission. Full authoritative scope, rules, architecture, ERD, API, security, UX, observability, acceptance, implementation and test checklists are in the linked documentation notes and C:\Dev\IdeaProjects\ChromaScape\docs\builderflow\sc-2150\full-plan.md. No Micro6 source/runtime, model activation or gameplay changes.

items.text: Include bounded upload/YouTube import, immutable media, durable bounded analysis, visible cursor evidence, manual review, catalog inspection and export within ChromaScape.
Exclude live input, Micro6 changes, exact tick alignment, physical-click inference, causal simulation, detector verdicts and model activation.
AC1 Given a valid bounded upload, when submitted, then one immutable source/original hash and playable proxy/index become inspectable.

AC2 Given a supported accessible YouTube video, when imported, then the canonical provider ID/acquisition metadata and exact downloaded digest are retained; unavailable/protected/live sources fail explicitly.
AC3 Given identical request UUID/body, when concurrently retried, then one source/job exists; conflicting content receives 409 without partial publication.
AC4 Given malformed/oversized/overlong/pathological media, when processed, then bounded failure occurs with no unbounded memory/disk/CPU or complete-artifact claim.

AC5 Given a qualified visible cursor clip and pinned tools/config/templates, when analyzed, then source-linked tracks/metrics meet the declared held-out threshold and repeated outputs have the same normalized hash.
AC6 Given hidden/unsupported cursors, overlays, crop/resize, cuts or frame-rate variation, when analyzed, then gaps and feature eligibility are accurate and unsupported observations remain unknown.
AC7 Given manual point/event corrections, when saved, then the original video/predictions remain immutable and the new reviewer/reason/base-revision lineage is resolvable.
AC8 Given imported footage, when training is requested, then no import/source declaration alone grants human or training eligibility; published curation and independent policy gates are required.
AC9 Given cancel/restart/lease loss at each stage, when reconciled, then no late/duplicate publication occurs, source evidence is preserved and cleanup/outcome is truthful.
AC10 Given another owner or unauthenticated caller, when requesting media/status/review/export, then access is denied without private metadata disclosure.
AC11 Given no native telemetry/alignment, when inspecting/exporting, then PTS/frame evidence is available but native ticks/physical clicks/hidden state are not invented.
AC12 Given catalog filters, refresh, keyboard navigation and error states, when used, then source/status/coverage are clear and existing native mouse capture/inspection still works.

AC13 Given browser/worker differing representations, when seeking/exporting, then original/proxy time mapping and hashes identify the actual frame evidence, within one source-frame interval on qualified ranges.

AC14 Given a bad-movement or human-origin claim, when shown, then it is supported by a separate reviewed source/report identity; tracker confidence never substitutes for detector calibration or human verification.

PA1 — Given multiple analyses, when media or source details are requested, then one owner/source-bound completed analysis supplies the derivative set without cross-analysis fallback; ORIGINAL remains source-scoped.
PA2 — Given concurrent controller and worker cancellation, when either settles first, then HTTP is truthful and no optimistic-lock 500, stale-generation mutation or false cleanup success occurs.

PA3 — Given malformed multipart input or configured byte overflow, when intake rejects it, then typed 400 or 413 is returned and reservations/staging are released; genuine storage failure remains a sanitized 5xx.
PA4 — Given process or decoder failure, when any public job/source/export representation is read, then stable bounded messages disclose no internal path or private diagnostics.
PA5 — Given unknown native targets, when the inspector renders, then uncertainty remains explicit and the native template regression passes.
PA6 — Given anonymous and independent local owners, when protected objects are accessed, then anonymous access is 401 and cross-owner source/media/job/review/export access is 404 without disclosure.

PA7 — Given limits, interruption, expiry, process escape, restart or competing instances, when work terminates or recovers, then ownership, containment, bounded resources and artifact publication remain correct.
PA8 — Given CFR/VFR input and frame caps, when indexing or deriving media, then exact PTS/timebase and complete-output checks prevent partial or invalid results from being published.
PA9 — Given a real browser and backend, when upload, playback, cancellation, review, correction, conflict and export flows execute, then the visible state and persisted revision/analysis agree.
PA10 — Given cursor-absent or ambiguous frames, when tracking and review run, then unknown remains explicit and no physical clicks, native ticks or training eligibility are inferred.

PA11 — Given approved held-out source-disjoint clips, when cursor qualification runs, then median error is at most 4 equivalent 1080p source pixels, p95 at most 12, visible recall at least 90% and absent-span false detections at most 1%.
PA12 — Given identical media, tools, configuration and templates, when analysis repeats, then normalized outputs and identities are deterministic; changed inputs create distinct identities.

PA13 — Given approved downloader pins and a public clip, when YouTube acquisition succeeds or fails, then provenance, quotas, constrained egress, cancellation and cleanup are verified without cookies or authentication bypass.

PA14 — Given all required implementation, acceptance and test evidence, when release is considered, then required gates have no unresolved failures or blockers and unsupported hosts/capabilities are not advertised.

FA1 — Given a Fedora verification run, when started, then isolated ports/database/storage/build outputs and a complete source/tool/input manifest make results attributable without altering the existing 8090 service.
FA2 — Given frame-index/observation reads, when paged or analysis-pinned, then only bounded owner/source/analysis-bound immutable data is returned and GET creates no work.

FA3 — Given a review retry, concurrent revision or invalid correction, when submitted, then identical requests are idempotent, changed bodies/stale bases conflict, and invalid frame/type/coordinate data is rejected without changing original predictions or old revision content.

FA4 — Given browser review, when corrections/source-use decisions are saved or conflict, then exact frame/analysis lineage is retained, unsaved work survives, and training eligibility stays false until the separate admission policy authorizes it.

FA5 — Given a restricted Fedora worker, when it attempts process escape, secret reads, network access or resource exhaustion, then enforced boundaries hold and publication/cleanup states remain truthful.

FA6 — Given supported visible/hidden/ambiguous cursor frames, when tracked, then exact source PTS, transform, hotspot, visibility and confidence are recorded without interpolation over unknown spans or cuts.

FA7 — Given declared supported observation cases, when analyzed, then visible action indicators, pauses, target-region/camera/activity estimates and cuts have source-frame evidence; unsupported semantics, physical inputs and native ticks remain unknown.
FA8 — Given identical media, method/config/tool/template identities, when analysis repeats, then normalized results match; changed identities create distinct analyses and never mix derivative sets.

FA9 — Given anonymous and independent owners, when protected HTTP objects are requested, then anonymous access is 401 and cross-owner access is nondisclosing 404 across source/media/job/analysis/review/export.

FA10 — Given a real browser/backend, when upload/playback/cancel/recovery/review/export and keyboard/narrow-screen flows run, then browser state, persisted revisions, bytes and selected analysis agree.

FA11 — Given crashes, expiry, competing workers, sweep or configured caps, when the lifecycle resolves, then leases fence stale work, admission is atomic, referenced bytes survive and incomplete artifacts are never published as complete.

FA12 — Given approved source-disjoint held-out clips, when evaluated once against frozen methods, then cursor median error is at most 4 equivalent 1080p pixels, p95 at most 12, visible recall at least 90% and absent-span false detections at most 1%, with the additional detector gates met.

FA13 — Given approved downloader pins/public clip and constrained egress, when YouTube acquisition succeeds or fails, then provenance, stable outcomes, limits, cancellation and cleanup are verified with no cookies/authentication bypass.

FA14 — Given all required evidence, when delivery is considered, then no required gate is waived, unsupported hosts/capabilities remain unavailable, rollback is rehearsed and tracker transitions reflect actual validation.

RA1 — Given the current dirty Fedora checkout, when verification starts, then isolated build/database/media/ports and exact manifests protect the existing 8090 service and make each result attributable.

RA2 — Given untrusted media workers, when they attempt secret/network/process escape or exceed CPU/memory/PID/disk/time/output limits, then enforced boundaries hold and readiness/publication fail closed.

RA3 — Given repeated or changed analysis/preview requests and competing workers, when dispatched or settled, then identities coalesce identical work, changed bodies conflict and only the current unexpired execution may publish.

RA4 — Given a source frame, when an exact preview is requested and read, then frame ordinal/PTS/index digest/transforms are pinned, pending state is honest, GET creates no work and referenced bytes survive sweeping.

RA5 — Given real browser corrections and concurrent revisions, when saving/retrying/reapplying/exporting, then drafts survive conflicts, original predictions and old revisions/exports remain immutable and training admission is not implied.

RA6 — Given declared supported visual cases, when analyzed, then cursor/action/pause/target-region/camera/activity/cut observations retain exact source evidence, confidence and unknowns without invented physical/native telemetry.

RA7 — Given anonymous/foreign owners, large artifacts, crashes, expiry, cancellation or competing instances, when APIs and lifecycle operations run, then access is nondisclosing, reads remain bounded and stale or partial results never become complete.

RA8 — Given approved source-disjoint held-out clips, when evaluated against frozen methods, then the existing cursor and additional-observation gates pass with coverage, counts and uncertainty reported.

RA9 — Given approved downloader pins/public clip, when acquisition succeeds or fails, then constrained egress, provenance, quotas, stable outcomes and cleanup are verified without authentication bypass.

RA10 — Given final evidence and all required hosts, when release is considered, then no required gate is waived, global check failures are resolved honestly and Felix/Shortcut reflect only successful validated transitions.

T2 PostgreSQL: clean migration plus upgrade from actual base, uniqueness, concurrent retry/conflict, fenced publication, revision races and immutable history.
T3 Artifact: streaming byte limits without full-file allocation, digest mismatch, simultaneous reuse, failure between move/DB bind, orphan/ref-aware cleanup and denied traversal/symlink.
T4 Upload: real small valid media, truncated/no-video/unsupported codec, false extension, quota/rate limit, disconnect and Range 200/206/416.
T5 Provider: fake adapter for deterministic success/removal/auth/rate limit/redirect/download overflow; real accessible controlled public YouTube video on release host, exact version/log proof.
T6 Isolation: arbitrary URL/host/port/userinfo, private IP/redirect/media protocol and config/plugin/cookie/exec injection refusal; no decoder egress or secret reads.
T7 Real-tool media corpus: fixed and variable FPS, dropped/duplicate frames, rotation/crop/resize, cuts, speed changes and proxy mapping.
T8 Tracking: manually annotated owned OSRS clips with visible standard/OSRS cursor, menu/overlay, occlusion and unsupported styles; held-out thresholds.
T9 Repeatability: identical tool/config/media on same supported build produces same normalized observations/manifests; cross-platform tool differences get distinct toolchain identities.
T10 Review: correction precedence, revision conflict/idempotency, reviewer authority, raw immutability, source-use/curation rejection and export lineage.
T11 Lifecycle: cancel/timeout/restart/lease theft before/during each stage/publication; owned process cleanup and slot release, late-worker refusal.
T12 API ownership: anonymous, foreign owner, forged audit header, authorized owner, private logs/title escaping, media/export access.
T13 JS/browser: import fields/limits, empty/progress/error/no-cursor/gap states, durable refresh, inspect/overlay/seek/review/export, keyboard and narrow viewport.

T14 Regression: existing MouseResearchService/worker/controller, MouseRecordingInspection, catalog JS, campaign/training/capture and replay artifact tests, plus Spotless/Checkstyle and scoped diff check.
T15 Supported-host smoke: upload and public-source import, inspect/correct/export, cancel mid-job, restart recovery and deny cross-owner media; record native commands and actual binary hashes.

RA1 Given the ordinary configuration, when the application loads it, then YAML has no duplicate key and both video intake and stabilization preserve bounded streaming behavior.
RA2 Given no trusted principal or a forged owner header, when any protected video operation is requested, then it is refused before reading private data or upload bytes.
RA3 Given active HTML/SVG disguised as video, when imported or navigated to, then it cannot execute on the application origin or be served as trusted inline media.
RA4 Given identical owner/request/file/metadata under concurrent retry, when registered, then one authoritative source/job exists; different bytes or metadata return 409.
RA5 Given a failure/crash at any registration step, when recovered, then no partial metadata graph or unsafe shared-byte deletion remains.
RA6 Given two workers and cancellation/lease expiry at any publication point, when transactions compete, then only the valid winner can finalize the complete analysis/ref/event/job result.
